messages:
devops-bot: ALERT: [region: ap-south1] control-plane unreachable for 4m, API healthcheck failures >= 5% - auto-escalation threshold hit :rotating_light:
jamie_ops: saw the alert. pinging oncall + starting triage. creating bridge.
lee_oncall: onit. first check: can anyone `kubectl --context ap-south1 get nodes`? my CLI times out.
suresh_sre: same, control plane API returns 502/504. no kubectl. checking controller-manager logs via cloud console.
maya_network: load balancer probes failing for control-plane LB. All masters show unhealthy in LB health checks. No recent config change from infra PRs.
jamie_ops: okay, reason possibilities: control-plane hosts down, network ACL change, or provider control-plane incident. I'll open ticket with provider. @aws-support can you confirm any control-plane disruptions in ap-south1?
aws-support: We're seeing an elevated number of API gateway errors in ap-south1 starting ~1876001000. Investigating.
lee_oncall: we should fail traffic away from ap-south1 for serving endpoints. Smart routing rule `region-preference` needs to push traffic to eu-central1/sfo1. Can someone flip the policy?
suresh_sre: I'll update routing weight temporarily. Setting ap-south1 weight=0 for production routes, add burst to sfo1 and eu-central1. Doing it now via internal console: `POST /routing/v1/policies/weight` payload applied.
jamie_ops: important: Dedicated pools in ap-south1 are isolated — will clients using Reserved capacity in that region see errors? We need to fallback to compatible model variants in other regions to avoid 503s.
lee_oncall: adding fallback policy: route -> compatible-model-variant -> other-region. Triggering rollout with canary 10% to verify.
maya_network: be aware cross-region latency for sync ops will increase. We should disable synchronous KV writes for now to avoid timeouts on client side. Pushing config flag `runtime.kv.sync=false` to affected routes.
suresh_sre: infra autoscaler in ap-south1 is failing to reconcile because control plane unreachable; we might see node eviction when control plane recovers. Let's pause automated evictions and set `prevent-eviction=true` via cluster admin hook.
jamie_ops: opened incident bridge: https://redwood-incidents/bridge/1876001234. Tagging oncall and infra.
lee_oncall: contacting customers with reserved capacity in ap-south1. Sending short note to customer-success to start outbound comms.
maya_network: quick checks: BGP sessions to provider seem intact. Problem localized to provider-managed control plane components per status.
aws-support: confirmed control-plane degradation. Raised with provider ops. Estimated next update 15m.
suresh_sre: running quick runbook steps: `curl -s https://ap-south1-controlplane/healthz` returns 504. `journalctl -u kube-apiserver` remote logs show `connection refused` from etcd endpoints.
jamie_ops: can we confirm etcd quorum? If etcd is degraded, restoring quorum is high priority. Any snapshot restore should be last resort.
suresh_sre: unable to reach etcd peers from control-plane nodes over internal network. Might be network partition inside provider.
lee_oncall: temp mitigation checklist: 1) Reroute serving traffic (done). 2) Disable writes that require control-plane (e.g., cluster admin ops) — notify dev teams. 3) Open support escalation with provider (prod-sev).
jamie_ops: cost note: traffic shift to other regions will increase egress and compute usage; finance FYI — this could bump next invoice. I'll estimate after we stabilize.
maya_network: will also enable circuit-breaker on client SDKs to avoid cascading failures, short TTLs for embeddings cache.
lee_oncall: we should stub a gradated rollback plan in case other regions start saturating. Activate capacity guardrails: max-per-region token rate = 70% of baseline to avoid OOM.
suresh_sre: posting quick command snippets for on-call runbook:
```
# verify control plane from jump host
ssh jump@ap-south1-jump
curl -v https://127.0.0.1:6443/healthz
kubectl --context ap-south1 get cs || true
```
jamie_ops: started incident timeline in tracker. Will mark P0 until control plane back to normal or failover fully complete.
aws-support: provider updated: root cause under investigation (control-plane network fabric). ETA 20-30m for mitigation.
lee_oncall: in parallel: run smoke tests against fallbacks. `curl https://api.redwood.com/samples/generate?region=sfo1` returns 200 for me. good.
maya_network: note: disable cross-region autoscaling until we confirm stable throughput. I'll patch autoscaler policy `cross_region_burst=false`.
suresh_sre: monitoring: watch etcd leader election metrics and apiserver request-latency. Alerts set to p95 latency > 1s.
jamie_ops: update cadence: every 10m until resolved. Next update 1876001294 (in 60s).
lee_oncall: acknowledged. sending customer comms draft to #customer-success for review.
aws-support: provider mitigation applied to some control-plane hosts, healthchecks improving but still flaky.
maya_network: seeing partial recovery in LB health. keeping routing weight at 0 until stably healthy for 10m.
suresh_sre: nodes still busy with kubelet reconnect churn, control-plane APIs sporadic. Noting a few 429s in request logs as other regions absorb traffic.
jamie_ops: create post-incident action items: review routing fallback thresholds, add circuit-breaker defaults client-side, and improve runbook for control-plane network partitions.
lee_oncall: I'll stay on bridge until stable. tagging @lead-eng in case we need product-level comms.
aws-support: final note for now: provider will continue remediation; we'll update in 15m or on substantial change.
